title: Yaakov the Sun, the Evening Prayer, and Light from Darkness

paragraphs.heading: Why Yaakov Lodged: “The Sun Has Come”
phrases: and he lodged there, for the sun had set” (Bereshit 28:11).
that the Holy One, blessed be He, caused to set
the orb of the sun before its time, etc.;
that my name is Sun?” etc. (Bereshit Rabbah 68:10).
taking “for the sun had come” as referring to Yaakov,
what sort of reason is this,
that he lodged there “for the sun had come,”
It is understandable according to what they said,
that He made the sun set before its time,
he was compelled to lodge there.
the meaning of the verse needs to be understood:
“and he lodged there, for the sun had come.”
אַךְ בְּמִדְרַשׁ רַבָּה אַחַר כָּךְ אִיתָא:
However, further on in the Midrash Rabbah it states:
you are the third leg, etc.;
there are no fewer than three” (Bereshit Rabbah 68:12).
that he is the entire holy Chariot,
and he is the ultimate perfection in the world,
for he is the one who bestows light upon the world,
namely the light of His holiness, may His Name be blessed.
And it is stated in the holy Zohar
Yaakov is the glory of the Patriarchs,
and he is the comprehensive whole of them all;
and because he is the whole of everything,
for Yaakov is the one who stands

paragraphs.heading: Three Patriarchs, Three Prayers
phrases: the prayers — the Patriarchs instituted them,
as written in the Gemara and the Midrash Rabbah (Berachos 26b; Bereshit Rabbah 68:9).
“to the place where he had stood” (Bereshit 19:27),
and “standing” means nothing other than prayer, etc.
His prayer is in the morning,
that there was no darkness whatsoever before him
veiling the light of His holiness, blessed be He,
and he was like one standing directly before the King.
when it is likewise still day;
and they learned it from what is written,
“And Yitzchak went out to converse in the field” (Bereshit 24:63),
and “conversing” means nothing other than prayer.
For before him, too, was bright
the light of His holiness, may His Name be blessed,
and he poured out his speech before Him,
like one who tells the King about his situation
and unburdens his whole heart before Him.
Yaakov our forefather, peace be upon him, however —
that he is the purpose of creation in the world
and the root of the entire Chariot —
שֶׁשְּׁמוֹ כִּשְׁמוֹ שֶׁל הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא,
for his name is like the Name of the Holy One, blessed be He,
“For Hashem God is a sun and a shield” (Tehillim 84:12)
שֶׁקְּרָאוֹ הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לְיַעֲקֹב אֵל וְכוּלֵּי:
that the Holy One, blessed be He, called Yaakov “El,” etc.:
“And He called him — Yaakov — El” (cf. Bereshit 33:20).
because he illuminates the holy Moon,
so that it shines even in the darkness of night.

paragraphs.heading: Cleaving in the Night
phrases: from the words “And he encountered the place” (Berachos 26b).
That is: even when a person is in darkness,
so that he cannot see the light of His holiness
even so there will avail him
so that he merits to see light
This is what it says, “And he encountered the place [HaMakom]”:
to the Holy One, blessed be He,
he is, as it were, truly
the light of the Holy One, blessed be He.
And this is what it says, “and he lodged there”:
that he instituted the evening prayer
“Who revealed to him that my name is Sun?”
And this is what it says afterward:
which they expounded in the Midrash Rabbah (parashah 70):
“From the wrath of the Holy One, blessed be He,
and they said in the Midrash Rabbah:
and to merit a great light.

editor_notes: P1: ר"פ in the Midrash quotation expanded as רַבִּי פִּינְחָס (Bereshit Rabbah 68:10: רבי פנחס בשם רבי חנין דציפורין), not ריש פרשה.
P1: מ"ה expanded as מַלְאֲכֵי הַשָּׁרֵת, per the Midrash text.

P1: the tarkosa / 'chevel nachalaso' Midrash is Bereshit Rabbah 68:12 (added to the English only). 'אין מפקיעין אותו' rendered 'cannot hold fast' (a cord of fewer than three strands); the sense of מפקיעין is somewhat uncertain.
P1: Zohar citation '(קסג ב)' expanded '(קסג עַמּוּד ב)' and given in English as Zohar I, 163b; in the Zohar line, דיעקב is kept as printed and read 'for Yaakov'.
P2: וכמו"ש before (סוטה י.) expanded as וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (a Gemara citation) rather than שֶׁכָּתוּב.
P2: 'ויקרא לו ליעקב אל' is the Gemara's (Megillah 18a) reading of Bereshit 33:20, not the Masoretic wording; vocalized as quoted.
